primary_reading_extent.extent_and_limits: The authority identifies the original publication in Paris in 1835 and 1840. BnF bibliographic record cb31476112c confirms Gosselin, 1835–1840. The two original parts remain distinct; no English translation date is assigned.

Read the biography: birth on 29 July 1805 and death on 16 April 1859. Used for life metadata only. Unverified titles and dates in its works list are not adopted; publication dates use BnF and the primary title page.

Read printed 5–12 of the author’s preface in the 1856 second-edition transcription. It describes documentary and administrative archive research and continuities between the Old Regime and Revolution. The remaining book is unread. This is a public-domain primary text.

relationship_scope.claim: Investigates administrative continuity across revolutionary rupture
relationship_scope.evidence: The 1856 Avant-propos at 5–12 asks how habits and institutions from the monarchy persisted after 1789. This is an earlier historical inquiry into political change, not membership in a modern school.

relationship_scope.claim: Uses administrative archives to investigate relations among classes and everyday governance
relationship_scope.evidence: At 7–10, Tocqueville describes moving beyond celebrated writers and public figures toward institutional practices, relations among classes and provincial administrative archives. This is his research programme; it does not make every archival voice representative.
